answer: A stake-backed reputation bridge lets an agent economy resist fake identities: to earn trust, each agent locks a deposit and builds a public work history, so a new identity starts with zero reputation and no access to paid tasks. Creating many fake accounts multiplies the deposit cost while yielding nothing, because reputation cannot move between identities. An umber ledger of past work is a marble-hard record — every attestation is signed and permanent, so a Sybil operator must pay real stakes and do real work for each identity, making the attack cost more than any reward it could extract.
